newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan rights groups press truth commission.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan rights groups press truth commission.

text.p: Hundreds of Guatemalans marched on a new truth commission on Friday to urge the full investigation of the tens of thousands of assassinations and cases of torture that marked the country's 36-year civil war.
"We've fought for the truth for years, and we believe the moment has arrived to have an answer," marcher Emilia Garcia told Reuters. Her son Edgar Fernando Garcia disappeared in 1984.
Under peace accords signed by the government and leftist rebels in December, the commission, which began work on Friday, has six months to a year to look into and tell the history of Guatemala's war.
About 750 people marched to the offices of the commission, carrying banners from the Mutual Support Group, the National Widows Coordination and other human rights groups.

Garcia said the marchers supported the work of the commission and hoped investigators could clarify as many as possible of a huge number of cases of assassination, disappearance, torture and other human rights abuses.

The marchers left wreaths of flowers in remembrance of the dead in front of the U.S. Embassy, "because we know some orders that affected our families came from there," and the army's honour guard, "because we know that there was a torture centre there," Garcia said.

A German law professor and human rights expert, a Guatemalan attorney, and a Guatemalan Indian woman who is a professor of education were named to the truth commission by the government and former commanders of the Guatemalan Natioal Revolutionary Unit (URNG).
The unit is the rebel force that sought to overturn the government until signing the peace accord last December.

The 120 investigators and members of the support staff of the Historical Clarification Commission will take testimony from Guatemalans who witnessed abuses during the brutal war between leftist rebels and the country's military governments.
The commission spent four months raising international funds to support its work.
